title: Semantic health can report ready without validating semantic service configuration
reasoning: The semantic service used by summarize/title depends on both an LLM client and provider API-key loading, but the health route only checks that container.llm_client exists before returning a ready payload. That can make GET /api/semantic/health advertise the semantic summarization service as ready even when provider credentials/configuration required by the actual semantic operations are missing or unusable.
recommendation: Align the health check with the readiness contract: either narrow the payload wording to say only the LLM client dependency is present, or validate the same semantic configuration needed by SemanticSummarizationService before returning ready.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this route, and the shown file has no route-level assertion that readiness covers provider/API-key configuration.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test where container.llm_client is present but provider key loading/configuration is unavailable, and assert /api/semantic/health does not report full semantic service readiness unless that is intentionally only a shallow dependency check.
minimumFixScope: Update health_check readiness semantics and add a focused route test for shallow-versus-full readiness behavior.
